message.content:
**Famous Dancers of the 19th Century**

| Name | Nationality | Notable Contributions |
|------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swedish-Italian | Pioneered the “en pointe” technique; star of *La Sylphide* (1832). |
| **Jean Coralli** (1799–1868) | French | Co‑director of Paris Opera Ballet; choreographed *Giselle* (1841). |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Master choreographer of Imperial Russian Ballet; created *Swan Lake*, *The Sleeping Beauty*, *The Nutcracker*. |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1815–1877) | Italian | Influential ballet pedagogue; authored *Principles of Classical Dance*. |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1884) | Austrian | Renowned Viennese ballerina; known for her virtuosity and dramatic flair. |
| **Enrico Cecchetti** (1850–1928) | Italian | Developed the Cecchetti method; teacher to many leading dancers. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Though born in the late 19th century, she rose to fame in the early 20th; known for *The Dying Swan*. |
| **John L. T. (John L. T.)** |  |  |

*(Note: The table includes dancers who were active or influential during the 19th century. Some, like Anna Pavlova, were born toward the end of the century but became prominent in the early 20th.)*
